chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hasan from al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Basir said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Fasting is not merely from food and drink, and it is incumbent upon a person to guard his tongue from vain falsehood during Ramadan and other times."
ai.seo_question: What is the comprehensive definition of fasting in Shia hadith beyond abstaining from food and drink?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expands the definition of fasting beyond physical abstinence to include spiritual discipline, specifically guarding the tongue from *al-laghw* (vain or false speech). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *siyam al-lisan* as a core component of the fast's validity, applicable not only during Ramadan but as a perpetual moral obligation for the believer.
